newsitem.title: INDIA: Three Indian states may follow Orissa power revamp.
newsitem.headline: Three Indian states may follow Orissa power revamp.

text.p: Three Indian states are considering restructuring their electricity distribution services to improve efficiency, power secretary P. Abraham said on Friday.
"States which are very closely following Orissa's experiment are Harayana, Rajasthan and Uttar Pradesh," Abraham, the highest ranking civil servant in the Power Ministry, told Reuters.

Last September, the eastern state of Orissa handed over management of power distribution to private firm BSES Ltd. The Grid Corporation of Orissa was set up to replace the Orissa State Electricity Board.
Orissa was the first Indian state to restructure its state-run electricity distribution services under India's economic reforms programme launched in 1991.
Low efficiency and uneconomic prices in state-run electricity boards have been major obstacles to foreign investors invited by India to meet its huge power shortages.
"Unless the electricity boards are made financially viable and they are made bankable, the investment that will come from the private sector will be limited," Abraham said.
He said the government planned to amend the electricity act to attract more private sector participation in transmission and distribution of power.
"These amendments will be carried out in order to have independent regulatory commissions," Abraham said.
Analysts say the independent authority would set the tariffs for rural, agricultural, domestic and industrial sectors.
Abraham said the amendments would be introduced in the forthcoming session of parliament, expected to reconvene next month.
"We would like to have these amendments during the budget session," he said.
